predecessors.note: The Han governor Liu Yu was killed; Cliopatria's Han shape of 184-196 includes the land.

land.text: You Province, 'covering present-day northern Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin and Liaoning' (End of the Han page); Liaodong was Gongsun Du's, so Liaoning is left out

successors.note: Yijing fell in April or May 199; the land passed to Yuan Shao's domain (written by this batch).

capitals.name: Yijing (fortress)
capitals.note: 'retreated to Yijing where he prepared strong defences'; the page gives no capital and no construction date, and the coordinates are approximate. His seat before 199 may have been at Ji (Beijing); the page does not say.

correction.text: You Province, 'covering present-day northern Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin and Liaoning' (End of the Han page); Liaodong was Gongsun Du's, so Liaoning is left out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 193-199; Cliopatria has no row and its Han shape (han-dynasty_184) is not cut. The infobox gives 'Inspector of You Province (self-appointed), in office 193 - March 199'; he also named inspectors of Ji, Qing and Yan (Yan Gang, Tian Kai, Shan Jing), claims the pages do not turn into territory. The page gives no frontier; Beijing, Tianjin and a 100 km circle round Baoding stand for You Province without Liaodong.

ledger.note: 193: Gongsun Zan holds You Province. He 'killed Liu Yu', the Han governor, and became Inspector of You Province, self-appointed (infobox: in office 193 - March 199); enfeoffed Marquis of Yi.

region.text: the Ji-You frontier: Yijing, Gongsun Zan's fortress, and the Hejian-Bohai country to its south

ledger.note: 193: the war with Yuan Shao over the Qing and Ji frontier. Tian Kai, Gongsun Zan's Inspector of Qing, was fought 'to a truce' by Yuan Tan in 193; Yan Gang, his Inspector of Ji, was captured at Guangzong.

region.text: You Province, 'covering present-day northern Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin and Liaoning' (End of the Han page); Liaodong was Gongsun Du's, so Liaoning is left out

ledger.note: 199: Yijing falls. 'In 199, Yuan Shao besieged Yijing'; Gongsun Zan killed his family and burned himself; 'Yuan Shao occupied Yijing ... in the 3rd month of Jian'an 4' (14 April to 12 May 199). His territories 'were completely annexed by Yuan Shao' (End of the Han page).

region.text: the Ji-You frontier: Yijing, Gongsun Zan's fortress, and the Hejian-Bohai country to its south

ledger.note: 199: the frontier war ends with Gongsun Zan's death at Yijing (3rd month of Jian'an 4, 14 April to 12 May 199).

region.text: You Province, 'covering present-day northern Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin and Liaoning' (End of the Han page); Liaodong was Gongsun Du's, so Liaoning is left out

ledger.note: 199: Gongsun Zan's domain ends with his suicide at Yijing; the infobox gives March 199 for the end of his office, the footnote's Gregorian conversion places the fall in April-May.

wars.name: Yuan Shao-Gongsun Zan war

zones.text: the Ji-You frontier: Yijing, Gongsun Zan's fortress, and the Hejian-Bohai country to its south

wars.outcome: Yuan Shao drove Tian Kai out of Qing in 193, besieged Yijing in 199 and annexed You Province.
wars.note: Panhe and Jieqiao (191) are named on the Gongsun Zan page without dates; the ledger's contest starts in 193, the first year dated on the opened pages.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for You Province; the shape is a stand-in of modern units.

notes:
Gongsun Zan, You Province 193-199. 4 pages opened (Gongsun Zan, End of the Han dynasty, Yuan Shao, Yuan Tan); no Cliopatria row.
Unsettled: (1) the 193 start is the infobox's term of office; the body gives no year for Liu Yu's death; (2) the infobox ends the office in March 199 against the footnote's 3rd month of Jian'an 4 = 14 April-12 May 199 (April used); (3) the capital: the page names only the fortress at Yijing; (4) the Qing and Ji claims (Tian Kai, Yan Gang) are not drawn; (5) the Liaodong of Gongsun Du (gongsun-liaodong) lay beyond him.
Counterparts: yuan-shao is written by this batch; han-dynasty exists.
